records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: saying: introduces the words that follow
decisions.reason: The usual opening of a speech from God in Leviticus, as in 1:1. The speech runs to the end of the chapter.

records.heading: Purification after childbirth

records.source: דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אִשָּׁה֙ כִּ֣י תַזְרִ֔יעַ וְיָלְדָ֖ה זָכָ֑ר וְטָֽמְאָה֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים כִּימֵ֛י נִדַּ֥ת דְּוֺתָ֖הּ תִּטְמָֽא׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel, saying, a woman when she conceives and bears a male, and she will be unclean seven days; as [the] days of [the] impurity of her menstruation she will be unclean.
pieces: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'When a woman becomes pregnant and gives birth to a boy, she will be unclean for seven days. She will be unclean just as she is during her monthly period.

L.2: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, 'When a woman conceives and bears a male, she will be unclean seven days; as [in] the days of the impurity of her menstruation she will be unclean.

R.2: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'A woman who has a baby boy will be unclean for seven days. It is the same as when she has her monthly period.

decisions.choice: conceives: becomes pregnant
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for seed and means to produce offspring, here to conceive a child. With "and bears" it covers the whole of pregnancy and birth.

decisions.choice: unclean: ritually impure, not sinful or dirty
decisions.reason: Unclean is a state that keeps a person away from holy things and the sanctuary for a time (verse 4); it is not a sin or a punishment for having a child (see 5:2; 11:4). Birth, like other flows of blood from the body (chapter 15), brings this state, and it ends with time and an offering (verses 6-8).

decisions.choice: the impurity of her menstruation: the monthly period
decisions.reason: The bleeding after birth is treated like the uncleanness of a woman's monthly period, whose rules are given in 15:19-24. For these first seven days she is unclean in the same way, and so is what she lies or sits on.

decisions.choice: a boy
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a male"; Balanced and Readable say "a boy", as verse 3 shows he is a son.

records.gloss: And on the day the eighth will be circumcised [the] flesh of his foreskin.
pieces: On the eighth day the boy is to be circumcised.

L.3: And on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin will be circumcised.

R.3: On the eighth day the baby boy must be circumcised.

decisions.choice: circumcised on the eighth day: the sign of the covenant
decisions.reason: God gave circumcision to Abraham as the sign of his covenant, to be done on every boy at eight days old (Genesis 17:10-12; 21:4). The law of birth sets it beside the mother's seven days of uncleanness: when they end, the boy is circumcised.

decisions.choice: the boy is to be circumcised
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the flesh of his foreskin". Balanced and Readable say only that the boy is circumcised, which is what the phrase means.

records.source: וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים יוֹם֙ וּשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים תֵּשֵׁ֖ב בִּדְמֵ֣י טָהֳרָ֑ה בְּכָל־קֹ֣דֶשׁ לֹֽא־תִגָּ֗ע וְאֶל־הַמִּקְדָּשׁ֙ לֹ֣א תָבֹ֔א עַד־מְלֹ֖את יְמֵ֥י טָהֳרָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And thirty day[s] and three days she will remain in [the] blood of purification; any holy thing not she will touch, and into the sanctuary not she will go, until are completed [the] days of her purification.
pieces: She is then to remain thirty-three days in the time of her blood purification. Until those days are over, she must not touch anything holy or come into the sanctuary.

L.4: And thirty-three days she will remain in [the] blood of purification; she will not touch any holy thing, and she will not come into the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.

R.4: Then for thirty-three more days her bleeding is being made clean. During that time she must not touch anything that is holy. She must not go into the holy tent until those days are over.

decisions.choice: blood of purification: the bleeding of the weeks after birth, a time of becoming clean
decisions.reason: The phrase names the later bleeding after a birth as part of her purification. After the first seven days her uncleanness is lighter: it is no longer like that of her monthly period, and the rules here forbid only holy things and the sanctuary. When the days are over she brings her offerings (verse 6).

decisions.choice: any holy thing: food or objects set apart for God
decisions.reason: Holy things include the priests' portions of the offerings and other sacred food (7:19-21; 22:3-7), which an unclean person must not touch.

decisions.choice: the sanctuary: the holy place of God's dwelling
decisions.reason: Here the sanctuary is the tabernacle and its court (see 19:30). An unclean person must not come into it (15:31).

decisions.choice: the holy tent
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the sanctuary" as the holy tent, the tabernacle where God was worshiped.

records.source: וְאִם־נְקֵבָ֣ה תֵלֵ֔ד וְטָמְאָ֥ה שְׁבֻעַ֖יִם כְּנִדָּתָ֑הּ וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים תֵּשֵׁ֖ב עַל־דְּמֵ֥י טָהֳרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And if a female she bears, and she will be unclean two weeks, as [in] her menstruation; and sixty day[s] and six days she will remain in [the] blood of purification.
pieces: If she gives birth to a girl, she will be unclean for two weeks, as she is during her monthly period. She is then to remain sixty-six days in the time of her blood purification.

L.5: And if she bears a female, she will be unclean two weeks, as [in] her menstruation; and sixty-six days she will remain in [the] blood of purification.

R.5: If she has a baby girl, she will be unclean for two weeks, as she is during her monthly period. Then for sixty-six more days her bleeding is being made clean.

decisions.choice: two weeks ... sixty-six days: each period doubled for a daughter
decisions.reason: For a girl both periods are twice as long as for a boy: fourteen and sixty-six days, eighty in all, against seven and thirty-three, forty in all. The law does not give the reason. Some link it to the boy's circumcision on the eighth day, which ends the mother's first period; others to the daughter who will one day bear children herself. Either way the offering at the end is the same for a son or a daughter (verse 6).

decisions.choice: blood of purification: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: The same phrase as in verse 4.

records.source: וּבִמְלֹ֣את׀יְמֵ֣י טָהֳרָ֗הּ לְבֵן֮ א֣וֹ לְבַת֒ תָּבִ֞יא כֶּ֤בֶשׂ בֶּן־שְׁנָתוֹ֙ לְעֹלָ֔ה וּבֶן־יוֹנָ֥ה אוֹ־תֹ֖ר לְחַטָּ֑את אֶל־פֶּ֥תַח אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֖ד אֶל־הַכֹּהֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And when are completed [the] days of her purification for a son or for a daughter, she will bring a lamb, a son of its year, for a burnt offering, and a young one of a dove or a turtledove for a sin offering, to [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting, to the priest.
pieces: When the days of her purification are over, whether for a son or a daughter, she is to bring to the priest, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, a lamb a year old for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering.

L.6: And when the days of her purification are completed, for a son or for a daughter, she will bring a lamb a year old for a burnt offering, and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, to the priest.

R.6: When her time of being made clean is over, whether she had a son or a daughter, she must bring two animals to the priest at the entrance of the meeting tent. She must bring a lamb one year old for a burnt offering. And she must bring a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering.

decisions.choice: a son of its year: a lamb in its first year
decisions.reason: "A son of its year" means a year old or younger, a young male lamb (as in 9:3; 23:12).

decisions.choice: burnt offering ... sin offering: the two offerings that end her uncleanness
decisions.reason: The burnt offering is wholly given to God (1:3). The sin offering cleanses (4:3): here no sin of the mother is in view, but the uncleanness of the birth, which the offering removes so that she may again come to the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: a young pigeon or a turtledove: the birds named in 1:14
decisions.reason: "A young one of a dove" is a young pigeon; the turtledove is a smaller wild dove. They are the birds allowed for offerings in 1:14 and 5:7.

decisions.choice: two animals
decisions.reason: Readable says first that she brings two animals and then names each one, to break up the long sentence.

records.source: וְהִקְרִיב֞וֹ לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ וְכִפֶּ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ וְטָהֲרָ֖ה מִמְּקֹ֣ר דָּמֶ֑יהָ זֹ֤את תּוֹרַת֙ הַיֹּלֶ֔דֶת לַזָּכָ֖ר א֥וֹ לַנְּקֵבָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he will present it before Yahweh and make atonement for her, and she will be clean from [the] spring of her blood. This [is the] law of the [one] bearing, for the male or for the female.
pieces: He is to present it before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and make atonement for her, and then she will be clean from her flow of blood. This is the law for a woman who gives birth to a boy or a girl.

L.7: And he will present it before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and make atonement for her, and she will be clean from the source of her blood. This [is] the law of the [woman] who bears, for the male or for the female.

R.7: The priest must offer it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and make atonement for her. Then she will be clean from her bleeding. These are the rules for a woman who has a baby, a boy or a girl.

decisions.choice: make atonement for her: remove her uncleanness so she may come near God
decisions.reason: To make atonement (1:4) here is to cleanse the mother from the uncleanness of birth, which is not a sin. The offerings restore her to the worship of God's people.

decisions.choice: the spring of her blood: the source of her bleeding
decisions.reason: A spring or fountain is a source of flowing water; here it is the source of the woman's bleeding (as in 20:18).

decisions.choice: law: instruction for one case
decisions.reason: The word means teaching or instruction. In Leviticus "this is the law of ..." ends the rules on one subject (6:2; 7:37; 11:46; 13:59).

decisions.choice: The priest
decisions.reason: Readable names the priest as the one who offers the animal.

records.source: וְאִם־לֹ֨א תִמְצָ֣א יָדָהּ֮ דֵּ֣י שֶׂה֒ וְלָקְחָ֣ה שְׁתֵּֽי־תֹרִ֗ים א֤וֹ שְׁנֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יוֹנָ֔ה אֶחָ֥ד לְעֹלָ֖ה וְאֶחָ֣ד לְחַטָּ֑את וְכִפֶּ֥ר עָלֶ֛יהָ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן וְטָהֵֽרָה׃פ
records.gloss: And if not finds her hand [the] sufficiency of a lamb, and she will take two turtledoves or two young ones of a dove, one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering; and will make atonement for her the priest, and she will be clean.
pieces: If she cannot afford a lamb, she is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean.'"

L.8: And if her hand does not find enough for a lamb, she will take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering; and the priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean.'"

R.8: A woman may not have enough money for a lamb. Then she must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons. One is for a burnt offering, and the other is for a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean.'"

decisions.choice: her hand does not find enough: she cannot afford it
decisions.reason: "Her hand finds" means she has the means. The law makes room for the poor, as in 5:7 and 14:21. Luke 2:22-24 tells that Mary brought this offering of two birds after Jesus was born.

decisions.choice: one ... and one: the burnt offering and the sin offering both remain
decisions.reason: Even the smaller offering keeps both parts: one bird is burned whole, the other is the sin offering (see 5:7-10).

decisions.choice: cannot afford
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the idiom "her hand does not find" means. Literal keeps the idiom.
